frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read is a MUSHROOM, not a ball cap. I measured both boards myself, alpha-thresholded row by row. Delivered front: cap max width 192px at row 175, then a 60px cliff to 132px at row 190, and the widest point of head-plus-hair below the cap is 144px (row 220) — head/cap = 0.75. Concept front view (spec box 86,391,129,871): cap max width 260px at row 246, head-plus-hair max width 271px at row 270 — head/cap = 1.04. That is a 29-point inversion of the drawing's own relationship: in the art the hair mass is the widest thing on the head and the cap sits down onto it; in the delivery the cap flares 33% wider than everything under it and background shows through the overhang on both sides in front, A-pose and the swing camera. Second defect, the bill: on the profile board the bill is a wafer of constant 8-10px section over a 58px projection (droop measured 24px over 56px = 23deg, so the 22deg droop and the 1.100 reach ARE fine as stated); on the concept sheet the profile bill is a contiguous run 41px thick at the tip (col 988) thickening to 66-68px at its root (col 946) over a ~44px projection. Normalised on head height (delivered 189px, concept ~254px) that is 4.2-5.3% section delivered against 16-27% concept — the bill is roughly twice as long and a quarter as thick as the drawing's, and in profile it reads as a knife blade or an antenna sticking out of the skull. The recorded note calls this 'a real forward duckbill'; it is not. Third: transitions are butt-joined primitives — shorts hem into thigh, sock into shoe, neck into collar are all cylinder-into-cylinder with a hard occlusion line, and the cap crown has a visible cone apex. Nothing is severed (no empty row inside the figure in any of the four boards) and the two legs are genuinely two legs.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The metered proportions pass and I re-took them: head height 34.6% vs concept 35.0 (delta -0.41, ok), head width:height 0.99 vs 1.05 (delta -0.06, ok), visible face left 26.6 vs 22.4 and right 27.1 vs 26.8 with asymmetry 0.52 (ok), ankle daylight 51.7 vs 56.9 (ok). So 6b.1/6b.3/6b.4 are green and rubric 3.13's aspect check passes. What holds this to 3 is the second half of the category — 'joints read as connected forms'. Cropped at 4x, the legs are smooth cones from the shorts hem to the sock top with no knee, no patella plane and no calf swell; the shorts hem is a flat cut with the thigh cylinder emerging from it; at rest in the A-pose and hero the shoulder is a soft lump and the sleeve is a straight tube to the cuff with no elbow form; the neck is a plain column meeting the collar at a hard ring. The concept's limbs are chunky toddler forms with an obvious calf and knee; the delivered limbs are markedly thinner relative to the torso even though the head ratio is in tolerance.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The worst category by a wide margin, and it is a construction failure, not a taste call. Band choice first: `npm run measure:strands -- calls_shot` at the DEFAULT 5-45% of head height reports concept 4.91 minima/row at prominence 16.9 against delivered 0.00 at 0.0 — 0% of count, 0% of prominence. But for THIS character the default band is crown-downward across the CAP (concept head 129-388, so the band is rows 142-245, i.e. cap dome to just under the brim), so its 0.00 is really 'the delivered cap dome has no panel seam and no texture', and on the concept side the 4.91 is partly cap seams and brim edge, not hair. I therefore re-ran on the rows where Theo's hair actually shows: 25-55% gives 0.84 vs 5.62 (15% of count, 159% of prominence) and 30-60% gives 1.14 vs 6.59 (17%, 176%). Those bands do reach the brows and the eye line, so some concept minima there are false creases (skin/hair and brow edges) — which makes 15-17% an OVER-estimate of what he carries, not an under-estimate. Cause verified in the builder, not inferred: `build_hair` in scripts/v2/blender/sculpt-theo-source.py uses `segments = 10` with `wave = 1.0 + 0.05 * cos(6 * theta)` — 1.67 columns per lobe against the ~4 Nyquist needs, and only 5% amplitude, so the wave is unrepresentable twice over. But the ratio is not even the real problem. `HAIR_LEVELS` maxes at `half_x = 0.455` while the skull's lateral half-width is `HEAD_RADII[0] * face_half_scale` = 0.400 x up to 1.08 = 0.432, so the entire hair shell is a skin-tight liner adding at most 0.023 (5%) of volume. The drawing's hair is the widest mass on the head (271px vs the cap's 260px); the delivery's is 144px against a 192px cap. Consequences, all cropped and looked at: the front board and the front A-pose board show TWO small dark triangular wedges at the temples plus two nubs below the ears and nothing else — no fringe, no hairline, bare skin across the whole forehead, temples and cheeks. In the four `-runtime-face-*.png` close-ups at 4x the hairline is a ragged sawtooth of dark specks along the cap edge that reads as dirt or stubble, produced by the piecewise `hair_window_z` step at |x|=0.42 sampled by only 10 columns. In `theo-runtime-swing.png` — a real gameplay camera, cropped at 5x — the back of the head is a small brown patch under the cap with a LARGE bare skin nape below it, and a skin-coloured ear form lying on top of the hair with a jagged seam. Rubric 3.3 bars a bare-skull read from any gameplay angle and requires the hairline to read from the front; both fail outright. The recorded note ('hair lifted to a legible deep brown with enlarged fringe wisps, ear-top flips both sides, and a covered nape in profile and swing views') is contradicted by the swing still it cites.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Three of nine measure:fidelity metrics are OFF and all three are the shoe: dominant tone of the band 88.4 vs concept 37.6 (tol 8), second tone 11.6 vs 61.4 (tol 8), mean saturation 13.6 vs 28.1 (tol 4). Cropped at 6x, the shoe is a near-white clog — a grey collar, three hairline lace straps, a tiny dark tick at the toe and a cupsole band barely a shade warmer than the upper; the concept's dark toe bumper and dark outsole edge are effectively gone. The sculpt script's own comment ('the charcoal saddle never reaches the bottom-9% window') and the recorded note ('shoe-band OFF cause accepted') explain the metric away, but the detector reads the CONCEPT's own pair as cream #ecddcc + tan #d9b68b at 37.6/61.4 — charcoal is not what it is comparing — and the saturation metric is independent of the split and also fails by 3.5x its tolerance. Second defect: the cap's cream team panel is a PAINTED GRADIENT, not a constructed edge. At front-board row 150 (cap 180px wide) the teal-to-cream ramp runs x196 (#9ea4a2) to x228 (#d7d2ca) = 32px = 18% of the cap width, per side; on the concept sheet at row 175 (cap 179px) the same boundary resolves between x197 (#39626d) and x202 (#fbedd0), i.e. under 5px = 2.8%. Six times too soft. Cause: `build_cap` colours 12 dome columns per vertex with `colour = TEAM_MASK if (frontness > 0.62 and z < 3.92) else TEAL`, so Gouraud smears the seam across a whole 30deg column. Judging TEAM_MASK on extent and placement only (not colour): placement is correct, centred front, but extent is over — the cream plateau is 45% of the cap width against the concept panel's 37%, and with the ramps the cream dominates ~80% of the cap face, where the drawing shows one crisp wedge of six. Third defect: in `swing_contact` five hard-edged cream parallelograms punch through the teal jacket back at mid-back; I sampled them at #bcb390 and #c1b99a against the jacket's #053d48, so they are cream-hued geometry (a tee or inboard sleeve ring emerging), not a teal specular — an interpenetration that reads at gameplay scale. Credit where it is due, which is why this is a 2 and not a 1: the jacket is genuinely constructed (separate shell with a fold-back front edge, a cream tee centre panel, cream sleeves, a striped rib hem, collar flaps), the socks have a proud roll with two crisp teal stripes, and the shoe does have a cupsole and lace straps.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The eyebrows are authored and invisible, and they are this character's signature. I opened `assets/v2/source/theo-face-atlas.png`: every one of the 16 cells carries a pair of thick black brows, and not one of them renders in any still — front board, front A-pose board, hero, run, and all four `-runtime-face-*.png`. The reason is geometric and the script states the numbers itself: the brow anchor lands at z 3.304, while the cap dome's lowest ring is z 3.290 with half-widths 0.650/0.595 and y_centre -0.030, so the cap shell sits in front of the brow row from any front-facing camera and swallows it. Cropped at 6x, `angry` and `grin` differ by mouth alone — the eyes and the (absent) brows are identical — and Theo's cocky arched brow, present in all five concept views, never appears. On the positive side: all four expression stills ARE genuinely painted, not stubs (294,526 / 295,659 / 297,025 / 296,299 bytes, within 1% of each other, no 29% empty-canvas file), and rubric 3.14 passes on its own terms — the grin opens with teeth, tongue shows a tongue, cheer opens, angry frowns, all legible at draft-card crop. The nose is a real form (`nose_push`, verified in the builder) and it does break the profile — but on the profile board it reads as a sharp triangular beak rather than the drawing's small upturned button, and the socket dish is so shallow that the eyes read as flat decals with a soft blur. A face-island seam is visible as a dashed scribe down the cheek just in front of the ear in the grin still. Ears are constructed, not bumps — `EarSpec(center=(0.020, 3.230), radii=(0.1550, 0.1650))` and `build_ear` are both present, and the profile crop shows a rim, an inner hollow and a lobe — but the form is a crescent flange with a hard dark notch behind it and, in profile, its front edge sits almost against the eye decal with no cheek between them.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Hero (`theo-runtime-hero.png`) does report `model model` at 28.5k tris, so 4.1 is satisfied and this is model evidence — but the read it delivers is 'a kid in an oversized two-tone bowl', with no hair and no brows anywhere on the head. Every distinguishing mass the drawing gives him except the cap is missing, and the cap's own shape is the mushroom described above, so at hero he is interchangeable with any other cap kid. The 40px strip on the board is a pale blob over a pale body with a darker band across the middle: the highest-contrast element in the concept — the black hair mop that in the drawing is 271px wide against a 260px cap — contributes zero pixels at 40px, so there is no memorable read left to survive (3.9 fails). hairMass.label: hair mass

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction

The concept's profile figure (tank-turnaround.png x731-929, shorts band y637-705) draws a hem, a side seam and a drape fold. The tee is better but thin: it has a collar ridge and a thin rolled sleeve cuff, and nothing else - no shoulder yoke, no side seam, and critically no bottom hem band (a 3x crop of the delivered profile torso shows the shirt bottom as a rounded blob edge, where the concept's same crop shows a hem band with a stitch line and a visible side seam plus fabric weave). Shoes are the one part that holds up: the measured shoe band split is 84.6/15.4 against the concept's 82.1/16.3 with saturation 24.8 vs 21.5, all in tolerance, and the midsole stripe and toe cap are modelled - but the concept's laces and velcro strap are gone.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: This is where the only OFF metric lands and it lands for exactly the reason the eye sees. measure:fidelity reports 'visible face right of centre' at 49.4% of head width vs the concept's 40.8%, delta +8.62 against a tolerance of 6 - that row is 62% down the head box, and the delivered reads as near-total bare skin there because there is no nose form, no nostril shadow and no lid mass eating into it. In plain terms the profile has a pinched wedge where the nose should be, and no lips and no chin at all. tank-profile-review.png also shows the eye as a flat grey-and-white sliver and the eyebrow as a black dash painted on the SIDE plane of the skull - a decal island visible edge-on - and tank-runtime-run.png shows the far half of the face as blank skin, so the decal covers the front plane only. Finally the identity is inverted: the sheet's signature is heavy-lidded droopy deadpan eyes with the upper lid over the top third of the iris under thick low wedge brows; the delivered has wide-open almond eyes with a fully exposed round iris under thin high arched brows. The one thing that saves this from a 1 is 3.14, which passes cleanly.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The clump term modulates RADIUS: x = half_x * clump(theta) * cos(theta), y = y_centre + half_y * clump(theta) * sin(theta). In an orthographic front or profile view the halo's outline at a given z is the extremum over theta of that expression, which lands near theta=0 / pi where cos(6t)=cos(10t)=1 for every row and every amplitude. So the outline is always half_x*(1+a6+a10) - one number per z-level, ten z-levels, ten straight facets. No amount of theta-modulation can scallop that outline; it can only shade the interior. The code comment's promised payoff ('grouped clumps with a scalloped silhouette instead of a smooth dome') is unreachable by construction. What Mimi needs is z-modulation (a per-row radius wobble, or real proud tufts) or an outline built from separate clump volumes, not a finer theta term. The halo is still roughly twice as column-locked as the drawing, and the raw top-K number that the last critic quoted (80.6%) is not comparable across the two images because K differs (3 vs 13) and so does its chance baseline. Chance-corrected, delivered 35.0% vs concept 17.4% over the default 5-45% band; effective columns 19.59 of 48 vs the concept's 44.60; 24 of the 48 bins carry ZERO creases in any row, while two bins (7 and 40 - the left and right shading rolloffs) carry 33% of all of them. On the tighter crown-only band (5-30%) it is worse: 15.14 effective columns of 48. Row-to-row persistence is 80.9% vs 82.7%, which looks like parity until you correct for chance (2.89 creases/row vs 12.67 gives baselines of ~17% and ~55%), after which it is 77% vs 61%. So yes: the minima DO wander with row now, exactly as the comment claims - they just have almost nothing to wander in, because the modulation never becomes a visible crease in the first place. The headline 23% is inflated by the band. measure:strands' default 5-45% of head height reaches down past the fringe onto the forehead and brows, and those hard skin/hair and brow edges are counted as strand creases. Re-run on hair only: 5-30% gives 19% of the concept's count, 5-20% gives 18%. The honest number for the crown is ~19%, at 116-156% prominence.

I could define it, so I did, and I ran the same detector over concept and delivered. Take measure-strands.mjs's own per-row crease detector (contrast-stretch the row to 0-255, smooth by 3, keep local minima of prominence >= 6) and, instead of only counting them, record each crease's position u as a fraction of that row's hair-mass width. Quantise u into 48 bins - one bin per mesh ring column. Then report three things: (a) TOP-K SHARE, the fraction of all creases falling in the K busiest bins where K = round(mean creases per row), reported against its own uniform-chance baseline K/48 and chance-corrected as (C - K/48)/(1 - K/48); (b) EFFECTIVE COLUMNS, exp(entropy of the bin histogram), i.e. how many distinct columns the creases actually occupy; (c) ROW-TO-ROW PERSISTENCE, the fraction of creases that recur in the next row within +-1.5 bins. A perfect flute scores 100% / ~K / 100%. A drawing of real curls scores near chance / ~48 / near chance.

My own luminance map of the concept confirms it exactly: the smile is the dark run at row 288, and rows 261-264 - which the sculpt script and featurelatitude.lint.test.js both cite as 'the small smile rows 262-270' - are his NOSTRILS (the nose bulb runs ~245-264). featurelatitude.lint.test.js's own header warns about precisely this failure mode ('...NOSTRIL not the lip line, so it reports the mouth 10 [points] high'); Noodle's hand-entered mouth: 69.4 is that mistake hard-coded, so the record's 'mouth 69.4/69.4 green' is the sculpt agreeing with its own error, not with the drawing. Eye-to-mouth spacing collapses to 11.4% of head height (iris centroid row 187.5, mouth row 207) against the concept's 25.3% (iris 233.5, mouth 288) - 45% of the drawing's - leaving the features crammed in a band under the glasses and the bottom quarter of the face blank. Expression: all four -runtime-face-*.png stills are genuinely painted and distinct (295-296 KB each, no undersized sibling - grin shows a teeth band, cheer an open O, tongue a pink tongue, angry a closed line), but in ALL FOUR the eyebrows are hidden behind the lens rims at the gameplay camera, so angry and neutral differ only by a flat mouth stroke and angry does not read as angry. At hero the near lens reads as a dark socket and the temple bar is the boldest mark on the face.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The single worst area, and the defect is specific. The concept's strongest facial feature after the hair is a pair of bold, thick, arched eyebrows sitting on bare forehead, clearly separated from the fringe in BOTH the front and profile concept figures. Trap 1 checked: the brows are not absent — every one of the 16 cells in assets/v2/source/turbo-face-atlas.png carries a heavy black brow, and sculpt-turbo-source.py:78 traces them to atlas rows 245-260. They are BURIED. The fringe is set so low over the face island that at 7x on turbo-runtime-face-grin.png and -angry.png only the bottom one-to-two-pixel sliver of each brow escapes the hairline, and it reads as part of the hair, not as a brow. The consequence is that the angry cell — whose entire signal is the angled brow, since its mouth is a small flat frown — does not read as angry at hero scale, let alone at draft-card distance. frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: DECAPITATED. I re-measured every board view myself: figure spans rows 73-647 (h=575px = 4.0ft) and rows 261-265 contain ZERO figure pixels in cricket-front-review, profile-review, front-apose-review and profile-apose-review alike — 5 rows, 0.035ft, at 32.7% of figure height. Row counts run 54,50,44,40,34,28,22,10,0,0,0,0,0,40,42,40 (front): the jaw tapers to a point, five rows of pure background, then the torso starts at a constant 40px. I cropped rows 215-295 at 6x with a magenta backdrop and the background is visibly straight through: the head FLOATS above a flat-topped neck stub. Root cause found in the sculpt source and it is arithmetic, not a posing artifact — HEAD_CENTER z 3.220 with HEAD_RADII z 0.460 puts the skull's bottom pole at z 2.760, while NECK_LEVELS tops out at z 2.720. 0.040ft of the boy has no geometry. Rubric 3.7 forbids holes and gaps outright and this is the worst shape on that list; silhouette.lint cannot see it because a gap open at both sides is never an enclosed pocket. Beyond the severance the large read still misses the sheet: the concept's profile is a radiating spiked mop over a clear cheek, jaw and ear, while the delivered profile is a smooth motorcycle-helmet shell with a hard flat-cut vertical back plane and an angular bevelled corner (a butt-joined primitive, which 3.1's 5/5 explicitly excludes), the torso is one bell-shaped apron slab from chest to hip ending in a hard hem ledge, and the sleeve meets the bare forearm at a visible diameter step with no transition. The one metric measure:fidelity puts outside tolerance is silhouette too: daylight between the ankles 26.7 delivered vs 0.00 concept (tol 12) — the bind stance is planted far wider than the sheet's feet-together stand. LEGS ARE NOT FUSED (3.12 is fine: clear daylight between thighs and calves in bind, A-pose and the run still) — if anything they are too far apart.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The RATIOS are fine and I took them myself with measure:fidelity: head height 32.7% of figure vs the concept's 34.2% (delta -1.48, ok) and head width:height 0.93 vs 0.87 (delta +0.05, ok), so 3.13's aspect check passes and this is not a bobblehead. What fails is the other half of the category — 'joints read as connected forms.' The head is not connected to the body AT ALL (see 3.1: 0.040ft of missing geometry between skull pole z 2.760 and neck top z 2.720), which is the most extreme possible failure of a joint reading as a connected form. It is not an isolated slip either: in the A-pose front board the shoulder is a square-cornered block with no deltoid — the tee sleeve is a fat cylinder that simply stops, and the bare forearm emerges from it a full step narrower with a visible flat ring at the junction. The hand is a paddle mitt. The neck itself is a bare flat-topped cylinder butt-joined to a flat-cut head underside, with no sternocleidomastoid, no trapezius sweep and no jaw shadow to bed it in. Ratios that measure correct on a figure that comes apart at the neck cannot score 4.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: I ran measure:strands myself at three bands, and the default 5-45% is not the culprit — the result is the same everywhere. 5-45%: concept 10.19 strand minima/row at prominence 24.4 over 98 rows, delivered 3.19 at prominence 72.2 over 70 rows = 31% of the concept's strand count at 296% of its prominence. Tightening to 5-30% to stay off the forehead and brows (where skin/hair and brow edges could count as false creases) gives concept 8.98 vs delivered 3.59 = 40% at 278%; 5-35% gives 9.34 vs 3.75 = 40% at 295%. The band choice moves the number by nine points and the verdict not at all. That count/prominence signature is diagnostic: the delivered mass has almost no creases, and the few it has are enormous — they are the facets of an 18-gon and the bases of the spike cones, not strands. I confirmed the mechanism in the sculpt source rather than inferring it: ring_loft_cap builds `segments = 18` columns and modulates them with `clump = 1.0 + 0.055 * cos(6 * theta)` — six lobes across eighteen columns is 3.0 columns per lobe, below the ~4 a crease needs to read, and the amplitude is 5.5% of half-width. That clump can never produce a groove; the code's own comment says it exists so 'the mop's back is not a featureless helmet,' and the board shows it failed at exactly that. What ships is a smooth glossy bowl with fourteen discrete cone spikes stuck on the crown, which reads as horns, not hair. Rubric 3.3 caps a smooth featureless blob at 4 'however correct its silhouette' — and this silhouette is NOT correct either. The concept mop radiates pointed locks in every direction, all round the sides and back; the delivered mass is a bare rounded shell everywhere except the crown mohawk. THE HAIR ALSO SWALLOWS FACE THE SHEET KEEPS CLEAR: CAP_FRINGE drops the lower edge to z 3.000 at |x| 0.44, and the profile crop shows two claw-shaped hair lobes hanging over the cheekbone down to mouth level with the near ear buried and the eye reduced to a sliver, where the sheet's profile keeps the whole eye, cheek, jaw and a fully drawn ear clear. I also cropped the profile hair at 12x around the temple and there is a genuine 4-5px dark pinhole notch in the otherwise unbroken shell.

clothingConstruction.note: The most defensible category, and it still does not reach 4. Real construction IS present and I verified it by cropping rather than asserting: the shoes carry a cream cupsole band, a toe cap, a lit collar and two-to-three lace stripes; there is a ringer collar at the neck; the ankle carries a rolled cuff ring; the bib carries a pocket badge. But the PRIMARY garment is a primitive. Cropping the torso at 4x, the overalls read as a single bell-shaped apron flaring from the chest and terminating in a hard horizontal hem ledge at the hip — no side seam, no leg-opening construction, and the two straps are flat plates butt-joined onto a flat bib with no buckle, no button and no topstitch, where the concept shows brass buttons on both straps, a bib pocket with a lip and a hip patch pocket. In profile the shoe is a bar of soap: a rounded rectangular loaf with no heel counter, no tongue, no toe upturn and a flat untreaded sole. The strengths are real: the eyes are the best-sculpted thing on the model, with a proper iris, pupil, highlight and lash line that read at hero scale; the freckles are present and placed as the sheet places them; and 3.14 passes cleanly. I checked all four -runtime-face-*.png stills and they are ALL genuinely painted, not stubs — bytes 275741 / 273942 / 274270 / 273929 for grin / cheer / tongue / angry, within 0.7% of each other, nowhere near the ~29% signature of an empty one — and I cropped and composited the four faces at 4x: grin is a closed curved smile, cheer opens to a red mouth interior with teeth, tongue puts a pink tongue out over the lower lip, angry drops the corners and angles the brows. At hero scale the character reads: the expressions land, the eyes carry, the palette (brown mop, green tee, blue overalls, taupe canvas shoes) is legibly Cricket, and the run and swing_contact stills show two clear legs, a bent elbow and planted feet with no visible tearing. I cropped the runtime hero head at 6x and the neck DOES read as connected once the skinning closes it, so the severance is a board defect rather than a gameplay one — but 3.7 is a board check and the board is the delivered evidence. At the board's 40-pixel strip the read degrades to 'brown bowl, green top, blue bottom.' The one memorable thing about this kid on the sheet is a wild spiked mop radiating in every direction, and the delivered bowl-with-a-crown-mohawk keeps only a fuzzy crown fringe of that at 40px — the sides and back go smooth and the read becomes generic against a roster of brown-haired boys. Add the sticker seam and the fringe overhang, both visible at hero scale, and this cannot be called 4.

polishFindings: BLOCKER — the head is severed from the body. 5 empty rows (0.035ft) at 32.7% of figure height in ALL FOUR board views. Repair is arithmetic: the skull ellipsoid's bottom pole sits at z 2.760 (HEAD_CENTER z 3.220 minus HEAD_RADII z 0.460) and NECK_LEVELS stops at z 2.720. Raise the top neck ring to at least z 2.78 (or add a ring that overlaps the skull pole) so the two forms interpenetrate rather than nearly touch, then re-run the board and drop cricket from the DEBT map in scripts/v2/continuity.lint.test.js — a debt entry is a defect that is still shipping, not an allowance.

The neck is a bare flat-topped cylinder butt-joined to a flat-cut head underside. Even once the gap closes, there is no jaw-to-neck transition, no trapezius sweep and no chin shadow — the join will still read as two primitives stacked.

Hair topology cannot carry a crease: 18 ring columns against a cos(6*theta) clump is 3.0 columns per lobe at 5.5% amplitude. Either raise segments to 24+ so each of the six lobes gets four columns, or replace the clump ripple with authored lock geometry. Measured result today: 31-40% of the concept's strand count at 278-296% of its prominence — a smooth shell punctuated by 18-gon facets.

The hair silhouette is the wrong shape, not just under-detailed. The sheet's mop radiates pointed locks from every side and the back; the delivered mass is a smooth bowl with all 14 spike cones on the crown. The sides and back need locks or the 40px read stays generic.
Profile hair back plane is a hard flat vertical cut with an angular bevelled corner — a visible butt-joined primitive at hero scale.

A 4-5px dark pinhole notch is visible in the profile hair shell near the temple (cropped at 12x from cricket-profile-review at left 255, top 120). Small, but it is a puncture in an otherwise unbroken surface.

The fringe hangs over the cheek. CAP_FRINGE drops to z 3.000 at |x| 0.44, and the profile crop shows two claw-shaped lobes covering the cheekbone to mouth level, burying the near ear and reducing the eye to a sliver — the sheet's profile keeps eye, cheek, jaw and a fully drawn ear clear.

The ear is built (EarSpec/build_ear confirmed) but does not READ as constructed on the board: at 14x it is a flat pointed flap with no outer rim, no inner shadow and no lobe against the skull. The source's own comment concedes the ears hide under the mop. 3.10 is about what the board shows, and it shows a bare flap.

The face is a decal island with a visible hard seam: at 9x the hairline is a right-angle staircase across the forehead and down the right cheek, with a tonal step between the decal skin and the sculpted skin below it.
The nose does not read in the front board view. nose_push is authored (max 0.086 tip push) but produces only faint shading where the concept shows a distinct round button nose with nostrils.
Eyebrows are flat dark quadrilaterals with cut corners, not tapered brow forms.
The neutral mouth collapses to a single thin stroke on the board. (The four expression stills are fine — 3.14 passes — but the default face is the one on the draft card.)
Shoulders are square blocks with no deltoid, and the tee sleeve meets the bare forearm at a hard diameter step with a visible flat ring — most obvious in cricket-front-apose-review.

The overalls are one bell-shaped apron slab from chest to hip with a hard hem ledge — no side seams, no leg-opening construction, no strap buttons or buckles, and no hip pocket, where the concept shows brass buttons on both straps and a patch pocket.
The bib pocket badge is correctly confined and correctly sized as the team accent (extent judged, colour ignored), but it is a flat rectangle with no pocket lip, so it reads as a decal.
The rolled ankle cuff is authored cream (CUFF #D5CDBE) where the concept's roll is light DENIM with orange topstitching — confirmed against a 4x crop of the concept's feet.
The delivered model adds prominent white tube socks between cuff and shoe; the concept shows bare skin at the ankle.

In profile the shoe is a soap-bar loaf: no heel counter, no tongue, no toe upturn, flat untreaded sole. The front view's lace stripes and cupsole are good and should be carried into the profile forms.
Two thin black hook-shaped slivers sit low on the front of both shoes (symmetric, so geometry rather than noise) and read as scratches at hero scale.

Bind stance is too wide: ankle daylight 26.7 against the concept's 0.00 (tol 12) — the only metric measure:fidelity flags. Read it as a stance note, not a tolerance to widen: the sheet stands feet together.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Two binary board items fail on measured evidence, so this cannot sit at 4. (a) 3.7 hole/gap: in lefty-profile-review.png the character's near lapel is SEVERED from the jacket by a column of alpha==0 (verified pixel-by-pixel, not eyeballed: y=290 x=238-242 all alpha 0; y=288-308, 21 rows, gap 3-6px). The same break shows in the front board at y=280 (2px). A second detached island sits at y=203-207, x=340-349 (a 10px hair spike clear of the mass). (b) 3.12 legs: the bind-pose board has ZERO rows of inter-leg daylight over the whole leg band (y 397-642); the concept's front figure has 105 such rows with a 56px max gap = 8.46% of figure height. The delivered thighs and calves are one fused navy trapezoid separated only by a shading crease. Separately, the concept's large read is 'backwards cap + long ponytail'; the front silhouette carries neither. The brim IS built (grepped: BRIM_REACH=0.660, build_cap's two-surface wedge) and it does project ~20px beyond the crown's rear in profile, but it is a 0.035-unit wafer entering the dome at mid-height (BRIM_Z_TOP 3.575 vs the cap's lower rim at z=3.400), so from the front and from the gameplay 3/4 camera the cap reads as a smooth beige helmet with no brim at all.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: The number wins and it is red: head width:height 0.88 delivered vs 0.98 concept, delta -0.10 against tol 0.08. I re-measured it independently off the front board (head box y 90-254 = 164px tall, max head run 146px) and got 0.890 — the tool is right. Rubric 3.13 is explicit that a head sculpted narrower than its concept never reads as the same kid, and that is exactly what happens: the concept's head is a wide near-circle, the delivered is a tall egg. Head height as %% of figure is fine (29.6 vs 28.4, +1.22 ok). Against that, the neck is a long straight column (see the 8x front crop) where the concept gives her a short child neck tucked into a hood collar, which pushes the read older. Joints are otherwise connected — shoulders keep a round deltoid in run and swing, no popped seams — and the legs' fusion is scored under silhouette, not double-counted here.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The weakest category. From the front board and from all four runtime face stills the head is a bare tan skull under a beige dome: the forehead is 100%% bare skin and the only hair is two ~3px yellow slivers at the temples plus a khaki wedge behind the jaw. I grepped before calling anything absent — FRINGE_WISPS exists (five entries, r=0.055) — so the correct finding is 'built but sub-visible': at 8x you can see exactly two gold specks at the cap's edge where the concept has a thick swept blonde fringe crossing the forehead. That failure is corroborated by the AUTO metric: visible face left of centre 34.2%% vs concept 27.6%% (+6.68, tol 6) and right 34.9%% vs 28.6%% (+6.28) — both sides show MORE bare face than the concept precisely because the hair no longer frames it. The mass itself is not one designed form: the pony is a hard-edged flat card with a chopped-flat tip and a straight vertical cut at the shoulder, and at swing_contact (4x crop) it swings across the front of the shoulder while the navy hood ellipsoid punches through it — a 3.8 interpenetration that reads at hero scale. Strand bands, stated: the DEFAULT 5-45%% band is invalid for this kid (head box 90-254 puts rows 98-164 on the CAP DOME; the cap's lower edge is ~y170), so its '8%% of concept strand count' is really a cap-panel measurement — true as far as it goes (the concept cap has six panel seams, a crown button and eyelets; the delivered dome has one smooth surface and a flat badge). At 45-95%%, where lefty's hair actually is, the delivered carries 55%% of the concept's strand count at 203%% of its prominence — few, over-hard divisions, i.e. slabs — but that band crosses the eyes on both images (the detector has no hair mask, it takes every in-figure pixel in the row), so I treat it as indicative only. Credit where due and I checked it rather than assuming: the authored hue separation DOES hold at runtime. Delivered hair hue 42 / sat 41 vs cheek hue 27 / sat 41 is a 15-degree gap, WIDER than the concept's own 32-vs-23; and against the cap (hue 34, sat 14) the 27-point saturation gap keeps them apart. The hue trick is not the problem; the missing fringe and the card construction are.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Genuinely constructed in places, and I confirmed each in the sculpt rather than guessing: build_lapels makes the tee window's edges real geometry (tubes, not a painted stripe), the shoe carries a cream cupsole, toe bumper and lace stubs that survive 4x, build_hood puts a real navy drape at the upper back, and a rolled jogger cuff exists in the leg profile. What holds it at 3: (1) the tee window itself is a PAINTED vertex-colour region, and its top boundary is a soft blurry diagonal gradient across the collarbone at 6x — a painted edge doing a collar's job; (2) the jogger cuff is authored CUFF #2E2F36 against near-identical pants, so a 'proud' cuff renders as no cuff at all; (3) the sleeves end at the wrist with no readable ribbed cuff and the jacket has no hem band or collar band; (4) the concept's cream piping seams down the sleeves and chest — a signature of the garment — are not present anywhere; (5) the cap, grep-verified, is CAP colour for both dome and brim with a single TEAM_MASK badge, so the concept's navy adjuster strap across the front and navy under-brim (the two highest-contrast elements that make the cap read as backwards) are unmodelled; (6) the same lapel that earns credit is the piece that floats free of the jacket in profile. TEAM_MASK extent, judged as extent and not colour: one badge-sized panel on the dome front, correctly modest.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The strongest category and a real pass. All four runtime-face stills are genuinely painted, not empty — 276.8/276.9/278.3/277.1 KB, within 0.6%% of each other, and visually distinct at 5x: grin is a closed-lip smile with a tooth band, cheer opens the mouth with teeth and a red interior, tongue puts a real tongue out, angry drops the brows to a hard angle over a frown. 3.14 passes properly — no cell collapses to a stroke, and the emotions separate at draft-card distance. Brows are painted in the atlas and carry most of the acting. Face left/right asymmetry 0.68 is clean. Held at 4, not 5, for two reasons rubric 3.5 names explicitly: there IS a visible decal-island seam — a straight horizontal band runs edge-to-edge across the forehead just under the cap at 8x, and it stays straight while the skull and cap edge curve, so it is the atlas island's boundary and not the cap's shadow; and the nose is a form in profile (it does break the outline) but on the front it is a nearly unshaded bump, so the features sit ON the skull's planes more than they are integrated into them. Note also that trap 4 does not apply here — the near-side eye in the 90-degree profile is foreshortened exactly as predicted, and I am not filing it.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero and field scale
heroAndFieldScale.note: The 40px read is fine — I built it myself off the front board and the orange/cream/navy tri-band with a blonde flank at the head is memorable and holds. The review page reports 'model model' at 26.9k tris, so 4.1 is satisfied and this is model evidence, not proxy evidence. What fails is the other half of 3.6, identity survival at hero and at the gameplay camera. lefty's concept identity is a girl with long blonde hair and a backwards cap; at the runtime camera she reads as a boy in a smooth beige helmet, because the brim is invisible from every forward angle, the fringe is sub-visible, and the pony is hidden behind the head in the hero, run and all four face stills. The one still where the pony is visible (swing_contact) is the one where it crosses the shoulder and the hood punches through it. Run and idle deformation are otherwise clean — feet plant, shoulders stay round, no tearing — so this is an identity failure at scale, not a rig failure.

NO FRINGE FROM THE FRONT (3.3): FRINGE_WISPS is built but at r=0.055 it renders as two gold specks at the cap edge. This is also the measured cause of the two OFF face-visibility metrics (+6.68 / +6.28), so fixing the fringe fixes those numbers too.

THE BACKWARDS CAP DOES NOT READ AS A BACKWARDS CAP: build_cap paints dome and brim alike in CAP, so the concept's navy adjuster strap across the front and its navy under-brim — the two highest-contrast elements of the reference cap — do not exist. The brim also enters the dome at z=3.575 (mid-dome) rather than continuing the cap's lower rim at z=3.400, and is 0.035 units thick, so from the front and the gameplay camera she wears a smooth beige helmet.

PONY INTERPENETRATES AT SWING (3.8): at swing_contact the head-parented pony slab crosses in front of the shoulder and build_hood's navy ellipsoid punches through it; the slab's tip is a hard flat chop, not a taper. Verified at 5x on lefty-runtime-swing.png.

PAINTED WHERE IT SHOULD BE CONSTRUCTED (3.4): the cream tee window's top boundary is a soft blurry vertex-colour gradient across the collarbone at 6x, doing a collar's job; the rolled jogger cuff is CUFF #2E2F36 against near-identical pants and so renders invisible; the sleeves have no readable ribbed cuff and the jacket no hem or collar band; the concept's cream piping seams are absent entirely.

VISIBLE DECAL-ISLAND SEAM (3.5): a straight horizontal band crosses the forehead edge-to-edge just under the cap at 8x and stays straight while the skull and cap edge curve — it is the atlas island's boundary, not a cap shadow. Caps this category at 4.

NOT DEFECTS, recorded so the next round does not re-file them: the four runtime-face stills are all genuinely painted (276.8-278.3 KB, spread 0.56%) and 3.14 passes with teeth and tongue; the hand is continuous with the sleeve (the multi-run rows at y285-317 in the front board are a tapered-limb artefact, checked at 8x); ears are constructed per EAR_SPEC and read with rim, inner shadow and lobe; the near-side eye in the 90-degree profile is foreshortened exactly as expected (trap 4); TEAM_MASK extent is one badge-sized panel, correct; the authored-by-hue blonde HOLDS at runtime, separating from skin by 15 degrees where the concept itself separates by only 9; the brim does project beyond its own crown (~20px); the 40px read is memorable; and the review page reports 'model model'.
